notes.title: Space Drilling Station looks fun for building and automation fans - with a new Steam Deck compatible demo
notes.content:
Space Drilling Station has you manage and automate a drilling station on a distant planet. The developer detailed their Steam Deck work with a new demo.

Read the full article here: https://www.gamingonlinux.com/2025/07/space-drilling-station-looks-fun-for-building-and-automation-fans-with-a-new-steam-deck-compatible-demo/

notes.title: Getting Space Drilling Station Playable on Steam Deck Was a Real Challenge!
notes.content: [p]Hello everyone![/p][p]Recently, I got a [b]Steam Deck[/b] as a gift, and of course, the first thing that came to mind was: "My game has to run on this!" I naively thought two short weeks would be enough: one for controls, another for testing. Spoiler alert: I was way too optimistic! 😅 [/p][p]After more than a month of work, I'm super happy to announce that I finally have a [b]playable demo on the Steam Deck[/b]! But let me tell you a bit about what went on behind the scenes of this adventure...[/p][p][/p][h3]🎮 Controls: Less Is More![/h3][p]At first, I wanted to use all of the Steam Deck's options: trackpads, joysticks, buttons... I thought it was awesome to exploit every possibility. Except, when playing, I quickly realized it was anything but pleasant. My "lazy" side took over, and I got tired of juggling between trackpads and joysticks. So I radically simplified: goodbye trackpads! I streamlined the controls to use only the bare minimum, making the experience much smoother and more intuitive.[/p][p][/p][h3]📉 The Performance Wall: Chasing Milliseconds![/h3][p]Once the controls were set, I hit the performance wall head-on. I knew my game wasn't an optimization champion, but on the Steam Deck, it was a disaster! I spent a good week tracking every millisecond, juggling parameters to find the right balance between fluidity and visual quality, and most importantly, to avoid draining the battery in less than 30 minutes. A real headache![/p][p][/p][h3]📜 The "Verified" Holy Grail: Valve's Requirements[/h3][p]Valve has very strict guidelines for the "Verified" badge. I had to face two big challenges: making all text readable from 30 cm away (you almost needed a magnifying glass before!) and removing all mentions of a mouse or keyboard. That meant redoing all the in-game videos and explanations so they were perfectly adapted to the Steam Deck. A huge amount of work![/p][p][/p][h3]🙏 A Month Later, Pride![/h3][p]More than a month after receiving my Steam Deck, I'm incredibly proud to have managed to solve all the issues. It's immense satisfaction to see [b]Space Drilling Station[/b] come to life on this machine. [/p][p]I sincerely hope you'll enjoy playing it as much as I enjoyed making it compatible. Please don't hesitate to give me your feedback; it's essential for continuing to improve the game![/p]

notes.title: Beyond the Station
notes.content:
[h1]Hello everyone![/h1]

A quick update on development: the past few months have been very [b]rich in advancements[/b]. The last playtest (a huge thank you again to the participants for their valuable feedback!) highlighted a few areas for improvement, notably [b]balancing issues[/b], a [b]somewhat simplistic planetary construction[/b], and [b]logistics and manufacturing management within the station that could become tedious in the long run[/b].

So, we've implemented several adjustments:

[list]

[*][b]Manufacturing and Logistics[/b]: No more daily adjustments! For manufacturing, you now indicate the desired quantity in stock. Logistics adopts the same logic: you define the desired quantity (or unlimited) to be deposited in storage blocks, replacing the old "collection point" approach.

[*][b]Overall Balancing[/b]: The balancing has been thoroughly overhauled for a much more satisfying result. Expect more measured production – goodbye hordes of handlers! The economy is also more demanding, which I hope will make the game more captivating. Contracts have been optimized for more transparency: you can now set your purchase price, thus influencing acceptance by other stations.

[*][b]Planetary Development[/b]: The planetary aspect is significantly expanding with new buildings. Pipes are making an appearance, allowing raw products to be transported through various separators and filters, optimizing refining within the station. Additionally, tanker drones will only be able to dock at storage buildings.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44120026/df0f35c6a4db4126082c221772b7bc01945b460a.png[/img]

[*][b]Planetary Mechanics[/b]: The planet is now composed of tiles. Building infrastructure on one of them grants you its control; of course, other stations can do the same. Resources are becoming scarcer, making control of certain territories crucial.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44120026/2c1e4b3f5b9795e9d0fc8800e6ce10386a044b8f.png[/img]
[/list]
Development is progressing well, and we truly feel that the bulk of the work is behind us!

Thank you so much for your patience and support!

notes.title: Devlog: A bit of history
notes.content:
Hello everyone,

The demo has been put back online to gather more feedback and address the few remaining issues here and there. Some time ago, Jean-Baptiste joined the project to handle the English translation. He brought many interesting ideas, and I decided to entrust him with the writing of dialogues and lore. He took over all the dialogues and a significant portion of the demo's texts. 
This devlog will focus on the lore and the campaign accompanying the early access. I'll now hand it over to Jean-Baptiste, who will present it all. Enjoy your reading.

Hello!!

I'm delighted to introduce you further to the universe of Station9. In this story, I aimed to explore themes of international cooperation, space exploration, and environmental sustainability. Every narrative choice has been guided by the idea that our ability to overcome global challenges lies in our unity and collective ingenuity. Station9 thus offers players the opportunity to engage in this extraordinary adventure in an immersive and engaging way.

In a distant future in 2052, humanity stands at a crossroads. Earth's resources are dwindling, the climate is changing, and our survival as a species is directly threatened. However, in this dark context, a glimmer of hope emerges when a meteorite crashes in Poland in the Białowieża Forest. Events unfold as scientists discover something new by studying its composition: Draxen, an energy source from the far reaches of space.

In 2056, the planet SE-20269.02, referenced a few years earlier and quickly renamed Promethea, turns out to have enormous Draxen deposits. This extraordinary, clean, and inexhaustible resource becomes the cornerstone of an unprecedented international effort to overcome the only obstacle, which is the distance. Located around a red dwarf YZ Ceti, also known as Luyten's Star, in the constellation of the Whale (Cetus), approximately 12.1 light-years from Earth.

In 2059, after three years of meetings, informal discussions, and summits, the OERS (Organization for Exploration and Space Research) is established, a partnership comprising the United States, Russia, China, the European Space Agency (ESA), and cooperating countries, India and Japan, representing 2.5 billion people in a world populated by 8.3 billion souls. Research is pushed in all directions in the following years. In 2062, the first spacecraft with an Advanced Ionic Propulsion engine integrating miniaturized fusion reactors with Draxen achieves four times the speed of light. In 2066, "TerraNex Station," the low Earth orbit spaceport, is inaugurated.

In 2078, the first drilling station is now operational, while other stations progress rapidly thanks to the experience gained with Station1. The exploration and exploitation of Promethea's resources enter a new era. We are now in 2082, and Station9 is about to be activated, and to answer your question: Yes, you will be in charge.

As you can see, I've spent a lot of time making the game's universe credible so that when you take command of Station 9, you can understand the events that led to exploiting a deposit on a planet located 14.21 light-years from Earth. These events are linked to the Station9 scenario.

Speaking of the scenario, it's progressing; the main plot is finished. The writing of dialogues and events is currently underway. 
That's it for today, all that's left is to wish you a happy and prosperous new year!

notes.title: Devlog: A productive summer
notes.content:
Hello everyone, I hope you had a great summer! 
After a lot of feedback on the Station9 demo, I decided to remove it from the store in order to improve it. So I'm going to take a step-by-step look at the changes I've made to the game over these rainy summer months.

[h2]Graphic Design[/h2]
Perhaps the most obvious changes are in the lighting of the various spaces. When I started developing Station9, the floors were smaller and the rooms more brightly lit. But by increasing the size of the levels and the number of objects visible on the screen, lighting consumed a lot of graphic resources, which is currently a major issue for 3D games. At first, I tried to compromise, but the result was really average. So I decided to set up a single light source for the entire space.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44120026/e089b65b6c739c367c2ba1c3802295df52e26b47.png[/img]

The performance problem solved, I was able to change the look of the floor. 
The rooms are about to get a little visual update: here are some objects before their texture is added!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44120026/4795e142afca3b892ea80a661fcb986c16636fc3.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44120026/fa1e089e79ac285cafc5faa83cd443d6d0f32b0f.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44120026/268112739a42d7dd7650b417ea9d2c46accaad82.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44120026/c7ef964390d96d2b185a1557ca728865e98239a7.png[/img]

[h2]Interface[/h2]
The redesign of the UI (User Interface: all visual components enabling players to interact with the game) was the other big project. The aim was to make it simpler and clearer. Thanks to feedback from the demo, I started to remove superfluous elements, replacing certain texts with icons where possible. I've also removed certain tabs to facilitate access to information on the game, in the tutorial for example. The experience is now much smoother and more enjoyable!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44120026/bf62fc2ac0e8b1b1d2788a4ed9c26d78ce74a616.jpg[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44120026/20e9223578ef6e7a508a339446177c90b050595b.jpg[/img]

[h2]Tech Tree[/h2]
The final major change concerns the technology tree. Previously, technologies were unlocked over time, and the tree was poorly organized. 
The player wasn't active: he or she simply had to start the process of acquiring a new skill or technology, then wait for it to be unlocked. 
To reduce this feeling of waiting, a research lab has been added. Assign researchers to it, and they will generate points that will be used to unlock the various technologies. The more researchers you have, the faster the points will arrive. 
The tree has also been reorganized, and after several attempts, I've opted for a fairly classic but effective layout. Tiers are now unlocked according to the level of your station.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44120026/81aaf484a973ab2ab553cd00a9e6566370899455.jpg[/img]

The new demo is currently being translated and I hope to be able to put it online in a few days. I can't wait to see the feedback on all these changes!

notes.title: New possibilities await you with update 0.11
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44120026/948a160e45daa62f8a14f4c31b0ef7565ed1c4b2.png[/img][h1]We're delighted to announce the arrival of update 0.11[/h1].

This update integrates new construction and manufacturing possibilities, while making the start of the game more pleasant.

- The Assembly block has been added to increase manufacturing possibilities, and new items can be made and exported.

- The length of the demo has been extended, giving you more time to enjoy the new gameplay possibilities.

- Blocks no longer cost money to make, they only consume resources and their construction time has been reduced.

- The employee shuttle now runs twice a day - having to wait a whole day for new employees was a real hassle.

- The technology tree has been rearranged so that certain technologies can be accessed more quickly.

- The night shift is activated more quickly, making the tutorial more pleasant and logical.

- Station customization makes its appearance. At the start of a new game, you're asked for your company's name, logo and color. For the moment, color is only used in the corridors, but as graphic elements are added, customization will take on its full meaning.

- Employee grades have been redesigned and brought to the fore. Depending on the infrastructure present in your station, the minimum grade of candidates is impacted. Some blocks require a minimum grade to be used.

Future work will focus on user experience, interface and ia.

Thank you for continuing to share your impressions and criticisms with us - it really helps!

notes.title: Update 0.1096
notes.content:
[b]Update 0.1096[/b]

Many changes and additions have been made to make the demo much better and more accessible. Modifications are still planned, but some additions couldn't wait.

[b]Fix:[/b]
- The volume of certain sound effects could not be modified.
- The list of applicants at the start of the game was unusually long.
- Various small corrections.

[b]Added:[/b]
- An option to adjust the interface scale has been added. The game should select the correct scale according to your configuration.
- To make the game more accessible, camera rotation and zoom have assigned buttons. 
- In panels, you can navigate between tabs using the Tab key.
- The tutorial has been modified and steps added to clarify certain points.

[b]Coming soon:[/b]
- A better save system.
- An improved market and ia of other stations.

notes.title: Hotfix Demo 0.106
notes.content:
Hello everyone!

While fixing a bug with the size of the Logistics panel affecting players with a resolution higher than 1080p, an error appeared making it impossible to open the panel. [b]This error is now fixed.[/b]

[b]Thank you very much for your feedback, it helps to make the experience better.[/b]

Fix:
- Translation errors
- Position and size of the Logistics panel
- Explanation about the red crosses on some blocks
- Various small code errors

Addition / modification :
- Color on the floor according to the utility of the block
- Reduced speed of movement of employees

notes.title: Hotfix Demo 0.1
notes.content:
Hello everyone!

Following the release of the demo, many bugs (some of which can ruin the game experience) have appeared. 
[b]Now they are almost all fixed![/b]

[h1]Bugs:[/h1]
- Abnormal behavior of the UI on some resolutions that prevent to click on the buttons.
- Logistic lines panel that doesn't work anymore after a hard closure.
- Option to disable dynamic shadows not working.
- The music volume does not turn off when you set it to zero.
- The Station panel creates errors when opened several times in a row.

[h1]Balancing:[/h1]
- Decreased export targets that were too often missed.

We continue to correct the problems to make the experience perfect.
